subject: Biotechnology
title: Biodegradable Plastics from Plants
description: A quick, practical guide to Biodegradable Plastics from Plants.

hook.text: Plastic pollution chokes the ocean — but some bacteria make biodegradable plastic naturally. Can plants do it too?

buildup.text: PHB is a polyester that bacteria produce for energy storage — it degrades completely in soil within months.

discovery.text: The PHB pathway genes transferred into switchgrass — the plant produces plastic granules in its leaves.

twist.text: Yields are still low — plants divert energy from growth to plastic production, reducing crop performance.

climax.text: PLA from corn starch fermentation is already commercial — 300,000 tons per year replace petroleum-based packaging.

punchline.text: Grow the plastic, compost the waste — plant-based polymers close the loop.

quiz.question: What is PHB?
options: A type of chemical fertilizer derived from petroleum
A biodegradable polyester naturally produced by some bacteria for energy storage
A plant hormone that promotes faster growth
